text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- Prime Mininster Nawaz Sharif announced that he would set up a fund with an initial capital of five billion rupees for youth schemes.
- The government will set up 60 special terrorist courts under the new anti-terrorism law.
- Algerian diplomat Lakhdar Brahimi starts a month-long mission to re-evaluate the U.N. role in Afghanistan.
THE NATION
- Special audit teams are visiting foreign and Pakistani banks to look into details of the foreign currency accounts.
THE MUSLIM
- Four persons, including a woman and a student, died due to heavy rains and floods in the mountains of Hazara division.
DAWN
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif urged India to dismantle the main barrier to bilateral ties and regional peace by resolving the lingering Kashmir dispute.
- The Mutahida (united) National Movement (MQM) rejected the Anti-Terrorism Bill 1997 which gave sweeping powers to the law enforcement agencies.
- Two young men, including a worker of the Pakistan Muslim League, were killed when a policeman opened fire on the crowd at the mausoleum of Pakistan's founder Mohammad Ali Jinnah.
- The Pakistan Navy has finalised a deal to export missile boats, Prime Minister NAwaz Sharif said.
- Opposition leader Benazir Bhutto has termed the anti-terrorism bill a black law which she said was unacceptable.
- Former Pakistani cricket captain, Imran Khan, ruled by a U.S. judge to be the father of a five-year-old girl, has offered to take a blood test.
- India has accused Pakistan of developing nuclear warheads for medium-range missiles with China's help.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The unsatisfactory law and order situation and violence are big deterrents keeping Japanese investors from expanding activities in Pakistan, the Pakistan embassy in Tokyo said.
